item.title: Prosecution Lays Out Case in Scicluna Murder Trial: 'There's a Body on the Street'
item.description: On day two of Lorin Scicluna's jury trial for the 2019 racially-motivated murder of Lassana Cisse, prosecutors played 112 emergency calls and walked jurors through the night the 42-year-old Ivorian father of two was shot dead on a dark road between Birżebbuġa and Ħal Far. Two police witnesses described arriving at Triq il-Ġebel to find victims Mohammed Jallow shot in the penis and Ibrahim Bah wounded in the backside. Defence cross-examination began Tuesday. Scicluna, 29, a former AFM soldier, has pleaded not guilty to nine charges including murder, attempted murder and a February 2019 hit-and-run that injured May Malimi. He faces up to life imprisonment if convicted.

Sources: Times of Malta

item.title: Unions Warn of 'Hidden Agendas' Threatening KM Malta Airlines After Minister's Remarks
item.description: Four trade unions representing KM Malta Airlines workers — the GWU, Union of Cabin Crew, Airline Pilots Association Malta, and Association of Airline Engineers Malta — have publicly expressed concern over Finance Minister Clyde Caruana's recent warnings of "hidden agendas" and "undercurrents" trying to derail the national carrier. The unions said such comments risk creating uncertainty for employees whose livelihoods depend on the airline, and insisted that "the future of KM Malta Airlines is a matter of national importance and should be approached with responsibility, transparency and mutual respect." They rejected any narrative that treats legitimate worker concerns as suspicious.

item.title: Audit Finds Government Board Members Paid Despite Holding No Meetings
item.description: The National Audit Office found that "in a few cases" board members on government-appointed bodies received their annual remuneration during 2023 even though no formal meetings were convened that year. The audit covered 462 bodies and 3,901 members, with around €9 million paid out in total; just over €500,000 of that could not be fully verified. Auditors also flagged incorrect board categorisations that overstated pay, deputy chairs underpaid at ordinary-member rates, and a handful of ministries that failed to submit documentation. The Cabinet office said it had completed a full recategorisation by March 2026 and tabled a revised manual in parliament in July.

item.title: Government to Spend €400 Million on Energy and Fuel Subsidies in 2026 — and Another €400 Million in 2027
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana told parliament that government expects to spend around €400 million on energy and fuel subsidies in 2026 — more than double the €172 million allocated in the previous budget — with a similar €400 million projected for 2027. Replying to a parliamentary question from Labour MP Alex Muscat, Caruana said international fuel price pressures are driving the increase and that there is currently no projected end date for the subsidies. He rejected calls from the Malta Chamber to begin phasing the support out, arguing that Malta's fiscal position is "completely different" from countries where recent protests have erupted.

item.title: Revolut Hit by Service Disruption Affecting Users in Malta and Across Europe
item.description: Revolut users in Malta and several other European countries lost access to parts of the fintech platform Tuesday morning, with all 30 services — including card payments, transfers and currency exchange — marked "partially unavailable" on the company's status page. The outage came as Google separately reported "multiple" Cloud services network failures across Europe. Revolut said its engineering team was "actively working to restore full service as quickly as possible." The disruption affected customers in Spain, Ireland, Germany, Italy and the UK, according to social media reports.

item.title: Magħtab Landfill to Be Dug Deeper for 2.9 Million Cubic Metres of Extra Waste Capacity
item.description: WasteServ has issued a tender to deepen the existing engineered Magħtab landfill from 10 to 54 metres — adding more than 2.9 million cubic metres of capacity, equivalent to 1,100 Olympic-sized swimming pools — without taking any additional land. The project will be carried out in two phases; excavated bedrock will be processed into construction products to offset costs, and waste removed ahead of excavation will be repurposed. WasteServ CEO Richard Bilocca said the goal is to make the best possible use of existing infrastructure while Malta works to reduce reliance on landfilling.

item.title: Court Expert: 'White Powder' in Mosta Drug Raid Was Cocaine and Washing Powder
item.description: Two men accused of trafficking more than a kilo of cocaine were actually in possession of 125 grams of the drug, while other white powder seized at their Mosta residences was probably washing powder, court chemist Gilbert Mercieca testified Tuesday. The substances were found alongside jewellery and mobile phones during a police investigation that led to the June charges against Justin Chetcuti, 33, and Jean Paul Spiter, 31. Both have pleaded not guilty and are out on bail. Defence lawyer Franco Debono appeared for Chetcuti; Nicholas Mifsud for Spiter.

item.title: Gozo Ferry Passenger Numbers Drop on Mġarr–Ċirkewwa and Mġarr–Valletta, Buġibba Service Picks Up
item.description: Passenger numbers on the main Mġarr–Ċirkewwa ferry fell 3.3% in the third quarter of this year compared with the same period in 2025, the National Statistics Office said Tuesday, while the Mġarr–Valletta fast ferry saw a steeper 9.1% drop in passengers despite running 5.8% more trips. The picture was brighter for the newer Buġibba and Sliema services launched in May: together they carried roughly 143,000 passengers in the quarter, with passenger volumes growing across all four legs from July through September. Total Gozo ferry trips reached 14,417 for the quarter, carrying 2,141,312 passengers.

item.title: Government says 86% of Budget 2026 measures implemented
item.description: Government has implemented 86% of the measures announced in Budget 2026, with the figure expected to reach 90% by year-end, according to a Budget 2026 Implementation Report presented to Finance Minister Clyde Caruana on Monday by Head of the Public Service Tony Sultana as preparations for Budget 2027 enter their final stages. Implemented measures highlighted 10 weekly pension increases for more than 100,000 pensioners, 160 million in tax reductions for parents, 15% stipend increases for 16,800 students and extensions of the Pink Card scheme to over-65s on Supplementary Allowance. The document covers measures announced in Budget 2026 and those carried over from budgets between 2022 and 2025.

item.title: Agius pointed gun at workers before shooting at police, court hears
item.description: John Agius pointed a gun at workers before shooting at police during a St Julians incident, a court heard on Monday, with a developer testifying that approximately 45 minutes passed between two episodes of gunfire before Agius eventually surrendered. The court also heard of long-running disputes over construction works adjacent to Agiuss property, particularly a dividing wall, with repeated complaints about contractors working close to his home. A forensic expert identified petrol among substances found in exhibits, and the case continues on November 23 and 30.

item.title: €930k EU-funded olive oil facility opens in Rabat
item.description: A new 930,000 olive processing facility in Rabat, financed under Maltas Common Agricultural Policy Strategic Plan, was inaugurated on Monday by ministers Keith Azzopardi Tanti and Anton Refalo. The project is expected to serve around 2,000 farms and olive growers annually, providing modern processing technology to improve productivity, quality and innovation in Maltese olive oil production.

item.title: Ex-soldier goes on trial for Malta’s first racial killing
item.description: Lorin Scicluna, 29, of Paola has pleaded not guilty before a jury to the 2019 drive-by shooting of Ivorian national Lassana Cisse Souleymane and the attempted murder of three others in Triq il-ebel, al Far. Prosecutors told the court that Scicluna, then a serving AFM soldier, and Francesco Fenech went to al Far to target people of a dark complexion whose presence in Malta they objected to. Scicluna faces life imprisonment if convicted.

item.title: Police alert suspected target in prison-phone murder plot
item.description: Convicted murderer Robert Agius and fellow inmate Damiano Torrisi were questioned about an alleged murder plot after police found mobile phones in their prison cells, with officers identifying and contacting the suspected target so precautionary safety measures could be taken. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said he had asked for a legal amendment to make possession of a mobile phone in prison a crime, prompting fresh opposition calls for an inquiry into how phones enter Corradino.
